name: load-failure-recovery
title: Load-Failure Recovery — Auto-Generating Default SED-ML (Planned)
question:
Can a default UTC (uniform time-course) SED-ML simulation protocol be
auto-generated for BioModels entries that fail to load with
"could not find a .sedml file in entry", recovering the 4/5 models this
investigation's own glucose-regulation run could not load in either
engine?

study_card.goal: For each MODEL* entry that fails with 'could not find a .sedml file', auto-generate a minimal uniform-time-course SED-ML wrapper (default duration/steps inferred from the SBML's own units) and re-attempt the COPASI/Tellurium load+compare.
study_card.mechanism: Planned: a SED-ML-synthesis Step that inspects a failing entry's raw SBML (time units, existing rate constants) to infer a plausible UTC duration/step count, writes a minimal SED-ML wrapper, and re-runs the same load+compare path glucose_regulation's composite already uses (LoadBiomodelStep + per-engine UTC + all-pairs nRMSE).
study_card.expected_result: At least some of the 4/5 models that failed in this investigation's live run (MODEL2001080002, MODEL1112110004, MODEL1806080001, MODEL2005050001) load successfully under both engines once a synthesized SED-ML is attached, expanding the COPASI-vs-Tellurium agreement sample beyond n=1.
study_card.main_expert_question: Is an auto-generated default simulation protocol (arbitrary duration/step count, not the model author's intended experimental design) scientifically meaningful to compare against, or does it only demonstrate loadability without a trustworthy dynamics comparison?
study_card.future_work: The real SED-ML-synthesis mechanism is not yet implemented. This scaffold's baseline placeholder reuses the existing glucose_regulation composite (which is what currently fails on these 4/5 models) purely so the study resolves and renders; the auto-generation/recovery step itself is future work.

biological_summary:
glucose-regulation's live 5-model run loaded only 1/5 models
(BIOMD0000000633, Bulik2016 hepatic glucose metabolism) successfully
under both COPASI and Tellurium; the other 4 — all non-curated `MODEL*`
BioModels preprint entries (Topp2000 beta-cell mass, Silber2007
IV-glucose, and two others) — failed identically with
"ValueError: could not find a .sedml file in entry". This is a load-time
packaging gap, not a numerical disagreement: the SBML itself is present
and biologically well-formed (these are recognizable
beta-cell/insulin-glucose models), but no SED-ML simulation protocol
(start/end time, step count, which species to record) ships with the
entry, so neither engine's UTC runner has anything to execute. Recovering
these models — by synthesizing a reasonable default UTC protocol from the
SBML's own units rather than requiring a hand-authored SED-ML — would
directly raise this investigation's load-success rate and let the
COPASI-vs-Tellurium agreement statistic generalize beyond a single model.
limitations: TBD — planned study, not yet implemented.

remaining_uncertainties: Why do most curated glucose models fail to load in both engines (missing SED-ML)? Can they be recovered?
